query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding moderate amounts of transition metals (e.g., Fe or Co) to Gd-based alloys will shift their Curie temperature closer to room temperature and enhance their magnetocaloric properties compared to undoped Gd-based alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Pure Gd-based metallic system without doping.
generation.intervention: Partially dope Gd-based alloys with transition metals (e.g., 5–10 at.%) via arc melting.
generation.conditions: Synthesize alloys by arc melting and measure magnetocaloric properties (isothermal magnetic entropy change) using standard magnetic characterization techniques (VSM or SQUID) near room temperature under variable magnetic fields.
generation.structural_mediator: Incorporation of transition-metal atoms into the Gd lattice, altering magnetic interactions.
generation.mechanism: The dopant atoms modify local exchange interactions and shift the Curie temperature, optimizing the peak magnetocaloric effect near room temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improvement in magnetocaloric performance at or near room temperature relative to the undoped Gd-based alloy, owing to the tailored Curie temperature.
generation.baseline: Undoped Gd-based alloys measured under identical field and temperature conditions.
generation.boundary: The doping level should remain moderate to avoid secondary phases or excessive broadening of the magnetocaloric peak, which would diminish the enhancement.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative gains in the magnetocaloric effect are not established by the current evidence; only the potential shift and improvement in the magnetocaloric response are supported by theoretical expectations.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate a series of doped and undoped Gd-based alloys under identical conditions using arc melting, systematically vary the transition-metal doping level, and measure their magnetocaloric properties near room temperature.
measurements: Microstructural features via microscopy (e.g., SEM, TEM)
Magnetization and magnetocaloric effect (ΔSm) measured with a VSM or SQUID magnetometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If doping with transition metals does not measurably shift the Curie temperature of Gd-based alloys or increase their magnetocaloric effect relative to the undoped reference, then the hypothesis is falsified.
